rounds.text: Ashnoor Textile Mills Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an extremely attractive P/E of 5.65x compared to a sector benchmark of 14.67x [E1, E6]. Furthermore, the stock trades at a price-to-book value of just 0.75x against a sector benchmark of 1.2x [E2, E7]. Fundamental value is heavily supported by a discounted cash flow model pointing to an intrinsic value of Rs 97 per share—leaving a substantial margin of safety of 48.0% against the current market price of Rs 50.6 [E43, E44]. Operational quality is robust, highlighted by a remarkable cash conversion ratio of 3.62x for Mar 2026 where profits were fully backed by cash, generating Rs 29 Cr in both operating and free cash flow [E34, E35, E36]. Profitability momentum is strong, evidenced by a 30% trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth and expanding operating margins reaching 15% against 10% three years prior [E21, E30]. Conceded: [E17].

Ashnoor Textile Mills Ltd carries fundamental vulnerabilities marked by a severe top-line contraction, with compounded sales growth dropping over 5 years (-1%), 3 years (-14%), and the trailing twelve months (-28%) [E15, E16, E17], culminating in an explicit flag for poor multi-year sales growth [E52]. Profitability metrics tell a similarly weak story regarding shareholder returns, evidenced by a low median return on equity of 6% over 3 years and dropping to 4% over the last year [E28, E29], alongside low figures for 3-year average ROE [E53] and recent TTM ROE [E61]. Furthermore, earnings quality is called into question because reported earnings include Rs 8.84 Cr of other income [E54], while the company refuses to return capital to shareholders despite repeated profits, showing a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] and drawing a negative flag for withholding dividends [E51]. Leverage is also creeping upward as borrowings increased to Rs 64 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 56 Cr a year prior [E38], paired with decelerating earnings growth signals [E60]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong TTM cash generation with Rs 29 Cr in operating and free cash flow [E35, E36], achieving a 3.62x cash conversion ratio where profits are fully backed by cash [E34].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over 5 years, 3 years, and the trailing twelve months reads negatively [E15, E16, E17], and multi-year sales growth is explicitly flagged as poor [E52]. However, the top line is turning around with a recent 7% year-over-year sales increase [E56] and operating margins expanding to 15% in the TTM from 10% three years prior [E30]. Conceded: median return on equity is low over 3 years and the last year [E28, E29, E53, E61]. Yet the company delivers superior efficiency compared to peers, with an ROA of 7.49% beating the sector benchmark of 3.37% and an ROE of 13.32% outpacing the sector benchmark of 7.19% [E8, E9]. Conceded: earnings include Rs 8.84 Cr of other income [E54] and dividends are zero [E4, E51], while borrowings increased to Rs 64 Cr [E38]. Despite these borrowings, cash generation is extraordinary, producing Rs 29 Cr in both operating and free cash flow with a 3.62x cash conversion that fully backs profits with cash [E34, E35, E36]. Finally, profit growth is actively accelerating with a 30% TTM jump [E21] and a sector tailwind score of +0.58 supporting the overall setup [E64].

Conceded: sales increased 7% YoY [E56]. However, this single metric masks a severe structural contraction where 5-year, 3-year, and TTM compounded sales growth read -1%, -14%, and -28% respectively [E15, E16, E17], officially categorized as poor sales growth [E52]. Conceded: ROA and ROE outpace certain sector benchmarks [E8, E9]. Yet the company’s actual reported ROE stands at a dismal 3.8%, with a 3-year median ROE of just 6% and a last-year median ROE dropping to 4% [E13, E28, E29], earning it an explicit low ROE flag [E61]. Conceded: operating and free cash flow reached Rs 29 Cr with a 3.62x cash conversion [E34, E35, E36]. Nonetheless, borrowings climbed to Rs 64 Cr from Rs 56 Cr [E38], earnings are artificially propped up by Rs 8.84 Cr of non-operating other income [E54], and the dividend yield remains locked at 0.00% despite repeated profits [E4, E51]. Finally, while the bull points to a 30% TTM profit surge [E21], the rules-based screen explicitly notes that earnings growth is decelerating alongside low profitability [E60, E61].
